 Civil Appeal No. 5465 of 2013
 O R D E R

1. The appellants in these two Civil Appeals are aggrieved by the Judgment dated 27092010 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh, whereby their first appeals seeking enhancement in compensation for the acquired land, have been dismissed.

entities.text: High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The State of Haryana issued Notifications under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, on 17041985 and 14101986 for acquiring land measuring 1.763 acres and 8 kanals, 6 marlas,
respectively, of Village Panjlasa, Tehsil Naraingarh, District Ambala.
The Land Acquisition Collector passed awards dated 2603 1987 and 30071990 granting compensation @ Rs.20,000/ per acre for chahi land and Rs.15,400/ per acre for barani land.
On a reference under Section 18 of the Act, the market value of the acquired land was assessed @ Rs.1,15,000/ per acre.
3. Still dissatisfied, the appellants filed first appeals before the High Court, which have been dismissed vide the common impugned Judgment.
4. It may be mentioned here that the land was acquired for the construction of Field Hostel for Drainage SubDivision at Naraingarh.
The acquired land is located near Naraingarh town.
5. For the purpose of evaluating the fair and just market value of the acquired land, the appellants relied upon three sale deeds (Exhibit `PA, Exhibit `PF and Exhibit `PH).
These sale deeds depict the market price of the lands ranging from Rs.2,08,000/ per acre to Rs.2,40,000/ per acre.

These Sher Singh vs The State Of Haryana on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34380803/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The High Court, however, was of the view that the sale deed (Exhibit `PA) was the most relevant exampler,
and the average price of the land as per the said sale deed comes to Rs.2,40,000/ per acre.
The High Court thereafter applied a cut of 50% on the premise that the said sale deed pertains to a plot measuring 10 marlas only.
The High Court thus held that the compensation granted by the Reference Court @ Rs.1,15,000/ did not warrant any further enhancement.
5. We have heard learned counsel for the appellants as well as learned counsel for the State of Haryana and perused the record.

6. In our considered view, the approach of the High Court in applying 50% deduction on the sale deed (Exhibit `PA) is erroneous in law for the reason that the acquired land is also not a big chunk of land as it is hardly 2 acres.
The sale instance is of 10 marlas and is in close proximity to the acquired land.
Even if it is to be assumed that a smaller piece of land is likely to fetch a higher market value, even then the cut of 50% would not be justified.

Considering all the sale instances relied upon by the appellants, the location and potentiality of the acquired land, the public purpose of the acquisition as well as the prevailing market value as was discernible from the exampler sale deeds, we are satisfied that the fair and just market value of the acquired land at the relevant time was not less than Rs.2,00,000/ per acre.
7. Ordered accordingly.

8. The appeals are, thus, allowed in part; the appellants are held entitled to compensation @
Rs.2,00,000/ per acre along with all the statutory benefits under the 1894, Act.
The enhanced amount of compensation shall be deposited with the Reference Court within eight weeks from today.
